title: The Bosphorus Brief — 28 September 2026
overview: A quieter Monday on the ground, though the diplomatic backdrop is noisy: a report of Israeli preparations for a possible ICC case against President Erdoğan is drawing attention, alongside a ruling-party resignation and steady progress on domestic and regional visa questions. For residents, the practical items today are travel and paperwork related — a possible Turkey-Saudi visa waiver, Montenegro tightening its own rules, and a reminder that ikamet checks continue nationwide.

sections.heading: ICC Report and Political Reshuffle
sections.body: Turkish Minute, citing Israeli broadcaster i24NEWS, reports that Prime Minister Netanyahu has ordered preparation of a possible ICC case against President Erdoğan over alleged treatment of Kurds and claims Ankara funds Hamas; the story is also carried by Middle East Eye and i24NEWS itself, all independent-leaning outlets, with no matching coverage yet in state or pro-government Turkish press. Separately, the ruling AK Party's deputy chair stepped down amid share-trading allegations, reported by ABC News, Bloomberg, and Hürriyet Daily News — worth watching for any market or governance ripple, though nothing so far touches residency or daily administration.

sections.heading: Visa and Travel Notes for Residents
sections.body: Turkey and Saudi Arabia are reportedly discussing a visa-free travel arrangement (tovima.com), which would ease movement for dual-based residents and business travelers if finalized. In the other direction, Montenegro says it will end visa-free entry for Turkish citizens from November 1, part of a broader move affecting Russia and Belarus as well — plan ahead if you hold a Turkish passport and travel there. Domestically, nationwide inspections in Kıbrıs (Cyprus) turned up six people without valid ikamet, a routine reminder to keep residence paperwork current.

sections.heading: Terror-Free Turkey Talks Continue
sections.body: The 'Terror-Free Turkey' steering committee holds its second meeting Tuesday, according to NTV Haber and Anadolu Ajansı. No major policy details have emerged yet; we'll flag any outcomes affecting civil liberties or security policy as they're confirmed.

sections.heading: Money and Prices
sections.body: The lira sits at 48.91 to the dollar and 55.74 to the euro. Turkey's central bank reserves fell $4.3 billion amid what Turkish Minute describes as fund market turmoil, and the OECD projects inflation staying elevated for longer, per Finimize — both worth factoring into budgeting for the months ahead.

sections.heading: Safety and Seismic Watch
sections.body: No new strong quakes near Türkiye since the M5.3 recorded September 24 near Hilvan; activity remains within the normal seasonal pattern. Travel advisories are unchanged: Türkiye at Level 2, with neighboring Syria, Iraq, Iran, and Lebanon at Level 4 — a good moment to double-check any regional travel plans against current guidance.

closing: Stay grounded, keep your paperwork close, and have a steady week ahead.
